statuses.running: To be done by the end of month {month}

dropped: Its boss left before it was done, and it left with them, in a box, with the plant.
formerBoss: Your former boss's Grand Plan: done

plans.title: One tool for everything
plans.what: Your boss's Grand Plan is a single new tool for the whole floor, which will solve all of its problems. Nobody has said which problems. Doing it properly will need the real figures, and only one person on the floor really has those.

needs.told: {who} had the real figures all along.

reaction.believer: Your boss opens the tool, finds the real figures in it, and reads them for some time without saying anything. Then your boss says that this is what it was for.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss opens the tool, finds a great many numbers in it, and closes it again. Your boss asks whether there is a version with fewer numbers, for people who are busy.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss opens the tool, sees your name on the launch e-mail, and thanks you in front of everyone. Afterwards your boss asks to be copied in on things in future. Before, ideally.

done.title: Your boss's Grand Plan: done
done.body: The new tool is in use across the floor, with the real figures in it. They are worse than the old figures, because they are the real ones. Your name is on the launch e-mail.

reaction.believer: Your boss says that it was a team effort, and names you twice, which is once more than you were expecting.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss reads out the launch e-mail at the stand-up, slowly, and seems pleased to learn what the tool does.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss accepts the applause on behalf of the vision. On the way out, your boss holds a door for you, which nobody has seen before.

done.title: Your boss's Grand Plan: done
done.body: The new tool is in use across the floor, with the real figures in it, and it is your boss's idea. The launch e-mail is from your boss. You are thanked in the last line, under the logo.

reaction.believer: Your boss opens the tool, reads the first page of figures, and asks you where they came from. You say. Your boss nods, slowly, as if filing it.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss opens the tool, sees that it is full, and says that this is what a single source of truth looks like.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss opens the tool, sees that the figures are flattering, and asks no questions about them, which is a kind of answer.

done.title: Your boss's Grand Plan: done
done.body: The new tool is in use across the floor, with figures in it. They are not the real ones. Whoever you asked sent what they had, which was last year's, with the dates changed.

reaction.believer: Your boss clicks the icon, waits, and clicks it again. Your boss says nothing at all, and then asks you, quietly, what it is for.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss forwards the launch e-mail upstairs with three exclamation marks, and adds the icon to the slide with the lighthouse on it.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss does not click the icon. Your boss forwards the launch e-mail upstairs under their own name, and tells you that this is exactly the kind of thing.

done.title: Your boss's Grand Plan: done
done.body: The new tool is live, as far as anyone can see. It has an icon and a launch e-mail. What it does not have yet is anything in it.

onPlayer.title: Lessons from the new tool
onPlayer.body: A write-up has gone round of why the new tool is not in use across the floor. It is two pages long, and your name is on both of them. Someone upstairs has replied that they would like to discuss it with you, and has not said when.

escapes.label: Say the Junior Associate ran the roll-out

worked.body: The write-up is revised. The Junior Associate's name is on page two now, and yours has moved to the acknowledgements.
worked.reported: Lessons from the new tool were assigned to the roll-out team.
worked.happened: You put the new tool down to the Junior Associate, who had been asked to make the icon.

failed.body: The Junior Associate replies with the brief you gave them. It was one line: Make an icon.

escapes.label: Reply that the write-up's findings are being validated

worked.body: The write-up goes for validation, to a team that validates things. It is not seen again.
worked.reported: Lessons from the new tool are being validated.
worked.happened: You sent the write-up to be validated, which is where write-ups go to rest.

failed.body: The validation team validates it, by Friday, and adds a page.

escapes.label: Wait to be told when
escapes.body: Nobody tells you when. It is on your record anyway.

onSomeoneElse.title: Lessons from the new tool
onSomeoneElse.body: A write-up has gone round of why the new tool is not in use across the floor. It was the supplier, who has been asked to leave the building, and has. The tool is now described as a pilot, and the pilot as a success.

results.reality: It was really done: the tool is in use, with the real figures in it.
results.appearance: It was done in appearance: it looked done from upstairs, and the figures in it were not the real ones, if there were any.
results.failed: It was never done, and someone had to be to blame.
results.running: It was still to be done when the run ended.

plans.title: Hot-desking
plans.what: Your boss's Grand Plan is that nobody has a desk of their own, so that everyone has every desk. Nobody's desk is to be touched until it happens, which is to be soon.

reaction.believer: Your boss books a desk, sits at it, and says that it works, in the voice of someone who did not think anything would.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss books three desks by mistake, and sits at the old one, which nobody has the heart to book.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss sees your name at the bottom of the booking system, and says that it is good to see people stepping up. It is not said warmly.

done.title: Your boss's Grand Plan: done
done.body: Every desk can now be booked, and is. The booking system is yours, and says so at the bottom.

reaction.believer: Your boss thanks you for doing the work, in private, and is clearly uncomfortable about the e-mail.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss reads the announcement aloud and is surprised by how well it has gone.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss takes the credit gracefully, and gives you the desk by the window, which can now be booked by anyone, and is booked by you.

done.title: Your boss's Grand Plan: done
done.body: Every desk can now be booked, and the announcement is from your boss. Your part in it is described as support.

reaction.believer: Your boss notices that everyone is at the same desk as yesterday, without the label, and asks you what has changed.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss walks the floor, sees no labels, and declares it a cultural shift.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss photographs the empty label holders for the newsletter, and does not ask where anyone is sitting.

done.title: Your boss's Grand Plan: done
done.body: The name labels are off the desks. Everyone is at the desk they had before, which is now nobody's, officially.

onPlayer.title: Hot-desking: a review
onPlayer.body: A review has found why everyone still has a desk. It was you, on page one. Someone upstairs would like a word about it, and has put it in the diary as a catch-up.

escapes.label: Say the Office Co-ordinator was to roll out the desks

worked.body: The review is reissued, with the Office Co-ordinator on page one. The Office Co-ordinator reads it, and says nothing, which they are very good at.
worked.reported: The hot-desking review found that it depended on Facilities.
worked.happened: You put hot-desking down to the Office Co-ordinator, who had been asked to order labels.

failed.body: The Office Co-ordinator sends upstairs the order for the labels, which is from you, and the labels, which say Hot Desk and are still in the box.

onSomeoneElse.title: Hot-desking: a review
onSomeoneElse.body: A review has found why everyone still has a desk. It was Facilities, who have been asked to reflect. Hot-desking is now described as a phase two.

results.reality: It was really done: every desk can be booked.
results.appearance: It was done in appearance: the labels came off, and everyone stayed where they were.
results.failed: It was never done, and someone had to be to blame.
results.running: It was still to be done when the run ended.

plans.title: A Centre of Excellence
plans.what: Your boss's Grand Plan is a Centre of Excellence for the whole floor. Nobody has said what it is to excel at. It needs people in it doing real work, or a sign on a door.

reaction.believer: Your boss walks round the Centre, sees work being done in it, and says nothing for a while. Then your boss says that this is what Excellence was supposed to mean.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss visits the Centre, and is puzzled that there is no ribbon. You offer to find one.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss visits the Centre, counts the people in it, and asks you whose budget they are on. They are on yours.

done.title: Your boss's Grand Plan: done
done.body: The Centre of Excellence is open, with your best people in it, doing the work that used to be done at their desks. It is going well. Your team is smaller.

reaction.believer: Your boss opens the door with the sign on it, looks at the chair with the cables on it, and closes the door again, quietly.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss has a photograph taken beside the sign, smiling, and sends it to Floor 3.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss does not open the door. Your boss forwards the launch e-mail to Floor 3 under their own name, with the word Delivered in the subject.

done.title: Your boss's Grand Plan: done
done.body: The Centre of Excellence is open, as far as anyone can see. It has a sign, a launch e-mail and a lanyard. What it does not have yet is anybody in it.

onPlayer.from: From: Lessons Learned, copied to Floor 3
onPlayer.title: Lessons from the Centre of Excellence
onPlayer.body: A write-up has gone round of why the Centre of Excellence never opened. It finds that it lacked leadership at team level, and names the team. It is yours.

escapes.label: Say the Programme Manager owned the Centre's launch

worked.body: The write-up is corrected. Leadership at team level is now leadership at programme level, which is a level the Programme Manager is on.
worked.reported: The Centre of Excellence was found to lack leadership at programme level.
worked.happened: You put the Centre of Excellence down to the Programme Manager, who had lent you the chair.

failed.body: The Programme Manager replies with the launch e-mail, which you sent, and the chair, which they would like back.

escapes.label: Say the Centre of Excellence is open, and virtual

worked.body: Upstairs is pleased to hear that the Centre of Excellence is virtual. A virtual Centre needs no room, and the room is given back.
worked.reported: The Centre of Excellence moved to a virtual model.
worked.happened: You said the empty room was a virtual Centre of Excellence.

failed.body: Your boss walked past the empty room every morning, and says so, upstairs.

onSomeoneElse.from: From: Lessons Learned, copied to Floor 3
onSomeoneElse.title: Lessons from the Centre of Excellence
onSomeoneElse.body: A write-up has gone round of why the Centre of Excellence never opened. It was Estates, who could not find a room. The Centre is now virtual, which is a kind of open.

results.reality: It was really done: the Centre had people in it, doing real work.
results.appearance: It was done in appearance: a sign on a door, a lanyard and nobody inside.
results.failed: It was never done, and someone had to be to blame.
results.running: It was still to be done when the run ended.

plans.title: One Roadmap
plans.what: Your boss's Grand Plan is One Roadmap: everything Floor 3 is doing, on a single page, in order. It needs someone to decide what stops, or a slide with no dates on it.

reaction.believer: Your boss reads the Roadmap twice, sees what has stopped, and says that this is the first one that could actually be followed.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss is surprised that it is shorter than last year's, and asks whether shorter is good. You say it is. Your boss says so too, to Floor 4's scaffolding.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss reads which programmes have stopped, notes whose they were, and sends the Roadmap upstairs with a covering note that does not mention you.

done.title: Your boss's Grand Plan: done
done.body: One Roadmap is done. It is on one page because things were stopped to get it there, and the people whose things were stopped have stopped speaking to you, mostly.

reaction.believer: Your boss looks for a date on the Roadmap, and then for a second one, and closes the laptop, gently.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss prints the Roadmap on A1 and puts it up outside the lift, where it looks like a Roadmap.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss sends the Roadmap to the Head of Transformation under their own name, with the subject line Delivered.

done.title: Your boss's Grand Plan: done
done.body: One Roadmap is done, as far as anyone can see. It is a single slide, and everything is on it, which is how you know that nothing has been decided.

onPlayer.from: From: The Portfolio Office, copied to the Board Office
onPlayer.title: Lessons from One Roadmap
onPlayer.body: A review has found that One Roadmap was never delivered because of a lack of clarity at middle-management level. Middle management is a level with you on it.

escapes.label: Say the Programme Manager owned delivery

worked.body: The review is reissued, with a lack of clarity at programme level. The Programme Manager asks for clarity on what that means.
worked.reported: One Roadmap was found to lack clarity at programme level.
worked.happened: You put One Roadmap down to the Programme Manager, who had asked you for the dates twice.

failed.body: The Programme Manager sends the review both of their requests for the dates, and your reply to each, which was a slide.

escapes.label: Say One Roadmap was delivered, as a roadmap

worked.body: Upstairs agrees that a roadmap was delivered, and that it is a very clear roadmap. Its being followed is a separate workstream.
worked.happened: You said a slide with no dates on it was the thing it described.

failed.body: Your boss had asked for One Roadmap to be done, not drawn, and says so, upstairs, with the slide.

onSomeoneElse.from: From: The Portfolio Office, copied to the Board Office
onSomeoneElse.title: Lessons from One Roadmap
onSomeoneElse.body: A review has found that One Roadmap was never delivered because the template was too small. A larger template is being procured.

results.reality: It was really done: things were stopped, and the Roadmap could be followed.
results.appearance: It was done in appearance: a single slide, with everything on it and no dates.
results.failed: It was never done, and someone had to be to blame.
results.running: It was still to be done when the run ended.
